requirements.statement: The Commodity details page's caption names the Description of the goods section, with the section number the service gives it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts Commodity details in its own section, 'Description of the goods', which also holds identification and additional details, and ruling 17 November keeps the section numbers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-006 and -p10-007 and repo-tests-p1-074 show the Description of the goods caption above the heading now, and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-010 records that no test depends on its number; trace-animals-fit-p9-003 captured the earlier 'About the consignment' caption (c-374).

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page has the title 'Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the heading 'Commodity details', the notification status strip above the caption, and an error summary titled 'There is a problem' above the caption and heading when it has errors.
requirements.why: The page's frame already matches Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-005 holds the heading and -p10-058 the service's standard error summary title, and trace-animals-fit-p9-002, -p9-004 and -p9-055 show the heading, the title and the summary above the caption today.

requirements.statement: The Selected commodities table on Commodity details has the columns 'Commodity code', 'Commodity' and 'Species', with a visually hidden 'Actions' column holding each row's Remove control. The Commodity cell holds the commodity's name and the Species cell lists the row's chosen species one per line, each but the last followed by a comma (for example '0102 | Cattle | Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'). The table and the 'Add another commodity' link sit above the questions.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows each commodity's name beside its code, and which of its species was chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table has 'Commodity code', 'Species' and a visually hidden 'Actions' column, with no column naming the commodity (repo-frontend-p10-010, -p10-011, repo-tests-p1-076); the species one per line with a comma, and the table above the groups, already match (repo-frontend-p10-012, -p10-165, repo-tests-p1-085). The commodity's reference-data name is already available to the page (repo-frontend-p10-015). trace-animals-fit-p9-010 and -p9-011 captured an earlier 'Common name' column (c-374).

requirements.statement: The Selected commodities table has one row per commodity, except for a commodity whose species the commodity list offers individually, where each chosen species has its own row, its Commodity cell naming the commodity and its Species cell that one species. Each row's Remove drops that commodity (or that one species) at once, with no confirmation, returns to Commodity details while anything is left, and goes to the commodity page when the last is removed, leaving the counts saved against the commodities that remain exactly as they were.
requirements.why: A trader can correct the selection from the details page without going back to the search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-018 to -p10-023 and -p10-170 show commodity-level and per-species rows chosen from the commodity list, Remove acting at once with no confirmation, the page coming back while anything is left and the last removal going to the commodity page (-p10-025), -p10-163 the surviving counts kept, and repo-tests-p1-085 the shared row for two species of one code. Each row's Commodity cell comes with the column req-105 adds.

requirements.statement: Below the Selected commodities table an 'Add another commodity' link goes to the commodity page, where the existing selection is still chosen, and saving a further species returns the trader to Commodity details with the quantities already entered kept and the new species' fields empty.
requirements.why: A trader can add a commodity without losing what they have.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-030 to -p10-032 and repo-tests-p1-087 show the link, the kept selection and the kept quantities.

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page's back link goes to the commodity page ('What are you importing?'), in the live-animals and the germinal products sets.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 Commodity details follows on from the commodity choice, and its back link goes there rather than to the reason page that precedes it in the step order.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's back link returns the trader to the overview the hub task came from (repo-frontend-p10-008, trace-animals-fit-p9-007, -p9-008).

requirements.statement: Opening Commodity details with no commodity on the notification sends the trader to the commodity page.
requirements.why: With nothing chosen the page has nothing to ask; the real service must not show an empty details page from Back, a refresh or a bookmark.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-024 redirects to the commodity question when nothing is selected, and -p10-025 shows the same on reopening after the last removal.

requirements.statement: Commodity details groups the questions under an h2 per commodity, '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)' (for example 'Horse (0101)'), and an h3 per chosen species naming it, with the type stepping down from the commodity heading to the species heading to the field labels, a section break between commodity groups and none above the save buttons.
requirements.why: A trader with several commodities sees which commodity and species each question is about, named as Design Release 2.1 names them.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each group's h2 is the bare commodity code with no name beside it (repo-frontend-p10-033); the species sub-heading, the type steps and the one visible section break per group already match (repo-frontend-p10-034, -p10-035, -p10-036). trace-animals-fit-p9-021 and -p9-022 captured an earlier '<common name> (<code>)' heading per species (c-374). How the species is named is the species label requirement's.

requirements.statement: Each live-animal species asks 'Number of animals' in a numeric text field with no hint; it is required ('Enter the number of animals') and must be a whole number of 1 or more ('Enter a whole number greater than 0'), each error shown in the summary and above that species' field and linked to it.
requirements.why: The number of animals is needed for every live-animal species, and Design Release 2.1 and the real service ask it the same way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-037, -p10-038, -p10-041, -p10-043, -p10-044 and -p10-169 hold the label, the empty description, the required rule and both messages, and repo-tests-p1-075 and -p1-083 prove them end to end.

requirements.statement: 'Number of packages (when required)', hinted 'Such as crates, bags or boxes', is asked for a chosen species only where the data fields page's package-count list names its commodity. That list covers bees; birds of prey (owls, falcons and other); cats; cattle; dogs; embryos or ova of cattle, goats, horses, sheep and pigs; ferrets; game birds (adult and day-old partridge and pheasant, and pheasant and partridge hatching eggs); goats; horses and donkeys; insects and other invertebrates, including the Asian hornet; domestic pigs and pig meat under safeguard measure; poultry (adult and day-old chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and guinea fowl, and chicken, turkey, goose, duck and guinea fowl hatching eggs); psittaciformes, including parrots, parakeets, macaws and cockatoos; domestic European rabbits and other domestic rabbits; reptiles; rodents; semen of cattle, dogs or cats, horses, goats, pigs, rodents or rabbits and sheep; domestic sheep; and SPF eggs. A species whose commodity is not on that list is asked only for the number of animals.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals data fields page is the specification for which commodity codes each conditional rule covers, and ruling 11 November ranks it above Design Release 2.1's demo commodity data on that; Design Release 2.1 still gives the field its label and its hint. A reference list is never a reason to block a row, so the question's coverage is not held back by the commodity list's content.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the question is shown for the commodity codes the frontend's own applicability rules name, read from its commodity service rather than from the specification's list, and a code they do not cover is asked for the number of animals alone (repo-frontend-p10-039, -p10-040, -p10-060, -p10-167: Bos taurus asked, ostrich not). Design Release 2.1 asks it of nine curated commodities only, which c-commodity-details-001 sets aside. Nothing in the end-to-end suite yet asserts the hint or the field's coverage (repo-tests-p1-089).

requirements.statement: For live animals the number of packages is optional, but when given must be a whole number of 1 or more, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes the field optional; the real service still validates what it stores, a constraint the prototype does not model.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-042 takes no required message for the field, and -p10-047 and -p10-168 refuse a non-whole number and anything below one with the same message, which repo-tests-p1-083 proves end to end.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals set the Commodity details error summary lists errors by question, all species for one question before the next: every number of animals error, then every number of packages error.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 orders the error summary by field type. Ruling 2026-10-09 splits this requirement per set and drops the mixed-load ordering, because a set holds one category; the germinal set's order is its own requirement.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-050 and repo-tests-p1-084-m1 list every number of animals error before any number of packages error now; trace-animals-fit-p9-057-m1 captured the earlier page-order listing (c-374).

requirements.statement: A species line that holds animal identifier records cannot be saved with a number of animals lower than the number of records: the error reads 'You have <N> identifier record(s) for <species> but entered <M> animal(s). Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.', singularised for one, shown against that species' number of animals field, its summary link going to that line's identification card, and checked only once every field-level check has passed.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the frontend is right to refuse a lowered count rather than orphan identifier records silently.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-054 to -p10-059 and -p10-058-m1 hold the message, its singular forms, the rule's conditions, the inline error, the link to the species' identification card and the walk that removes a record and carries on.

requirements.statement: Commodity details fills each field with the quantity already saved, and after a validation error re-shows the page with every entered value kept, trimmed of surrounding spaces, each summary link moving focus to its own field.
requirements.why: A trader never retypes what they entered; ruling 26 October keeps what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-062 pre-fills the stored counts, -p10-051, -p10-052 and -p10-053 keep what was typed on a refused save and move focus to the named field, and -p10-061 trims the values before they are checked and stored.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, reached in the journey from the main import reason page, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details goes to Identification details when any chosen species needs identifiers, otherwise to Additional details when that page applies, otherwise to the arrival details; opened from its overview task it returns to the overview.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 Commodity details is a step of the journey that leads on to the next one; ruling 2026-10-09 keeps a page opened from its overview task returning to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-066 sends a saved page to the next page the journey puts after it and -p10-065 shows that next page as Identification details; trace-animals-fit-p9-035 captured the earlier hop to the overview (c-374).

requirements.statement: In the journey, Commodity details comes after the main import reason page and before identification, additional and arrival details, and stays the set's own consignment-details journey page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the reason for import between choosing commodities and giving their details; the page's real path is the service's architecture, which the prototype does not decide.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-066 carries Commodity details on to the next journey page and repo-tests-p1-073 addresses it at the set's consignment-details page; trace-animals-fit-p9-001 captured the earlier hop straight from the commodity page (c-374).

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on Commodity details validates the page in full first, making the same checks as 'Save and continue'; once valid it saves and goes to the overview (to check answers when amending). 'Cancel and return to overview' goes to the overview without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not save invalid quantities on a soft save, and rulings 26 October and 27 November make the two save buttons run the same checks. DR1's rule (b) gives a page the overview links to all three return controls.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-063 ends the page with the three controls, -p10-064 and repo-tests-p1-080 show a valid soft save stored and the trader returned to the overview, -p10-053 the refused page served at 400, trace-animals-fit-p9-033 the cancel link to the overview, and ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-012 records that both save buttons already make the same checks.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals set the overview's Commodity details task shows Complete only when every chosen species has a valid number of animals; with no species chosen it is not complete.
requirements.why: The task status tells the trader what is left to do. Ruling 2026-10-09 splits this requirement per set and drops the mixed-load temperature condition; the germinal set's condition is its own requirement.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-039 and -p9-043 show the task Complete once every line holds a valid count and To do with commodities chosen but no counts, and repo-frontend-p1-031 that the page adds no obligation of its own beyond the lines' counts.

requirements.statement: The commodity page and Commodity details have no serious or critical axe violations under the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags, empty, with results and a selection on screen, and in their error states.
requirements.why: The pages must stay accessible as they change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-067 checks Commodity details with and without errors shown and finds no serious or critical violation; the commodity page's own check is weighed with that page.

requirements.statement: Where Design Release 2.1 uses custom markup that looks the same as a GOV.UK component (its caption and heading classes, section breaks, the div-grid Selected commodities list, the link-styled Remove buttons, the button wrappers), the real pages keep the GOV.UK component: caption, heading, section break, Table and Button group.
requirements.why: The real services stay inside the govuk-frontend toolbox; the custom classes change nothing a user can see.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-075 shows the page built from govuk-frontend components apart from app-journey-strip and app-link-button today (-p9-006, -p9-013).

requirements.statement: Every form on the commodity page and Commodity details (the quantities form and the Remove table form) posts the CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, with the browser's own validation switched off so every refusal is the service's own message.
requirements.why: Saves must be protected against forged posts and against two sessions overwriting each other, a real persistence constraint the prototype does not model, and server-side checks must be the only ones a trader meets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-156 carries the crumb and the concurrency token on Commodity details' forms, and -p10-157 turns the browser's validation off.

requirements.statement: Pressing Remove on Commodity details keeps the numbers the trader has typed on the page but not yet saved, so they are still in their fields when the page comes back, and a surviving line the post names no count for shows its stored value instead.
requirements.why: Ruling 26 October states that what a trader typed is never dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-028 and repo-tests-p1-086 show the typed-but-unsaved counts kept after a removal now, and repo-frontend-p10-029 the surviving line falling back to its stored value with a warning logged; trace-animals-fit-p9-068 captured the earlier loss (c-374).

requirements.statement: Commodity details shows no total of animals or packages; the numbers saved on it are what the overview adds up into its commodity totals (for example '27 Animals' and '6 Packages/boxes').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 works the totals out for the overview only; the trader sees them there.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-078 shows no totals on the page and trace-animals-fit-p9-040 shows the overview summing them today.

requirements.statement: On the germinal products set the overview's Commodity details task shows Complete only when every chosen species has a valid quantity, the count the page makes mandatory (a whole number of 1 or more, within its limit), and every optional answer entered on the page is valid; an optional answer left blank, the temperature included, does not hold it back. With no species chosen it is not complete.
requirements.why: The task status tells the trader what is left to do; ruling 2026-10-09 splits req-126 per set. Design Release 2.1 counts the quantity and not the optional number of packages, and the data fields page makes the quantity mandatory to proceed and temperature optional (c-232), so Design Release 2.1's temperature bar is not built.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's 'Commodities in the consignment' list (its table of Category, Genus or variety and Quantity, the Change and Remove actions, 'Add another commodity', the 'Commodities removed' banner, the 'Add at least one commodity' floor and its Save and continue alone) stays as it is.
requirements.why: Out of scope: no row in this area changes the plants commodities list, which has no animals or Design Release 2.1 counterpart in the form plants has it. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon changes plants only where a row changes a page or behaviour plants also has, and plants keeps its own questions, answers, sections, step order and data; Design Release 2.1 covers the animals commodity search and Commodity details, which plants does not have. Where plants already follows the same pattern (removing a line at once with no confirmation, 'Add another commodity', keeping entered values after an error, carrying the change context), it stays as it is. The list offers 'Save and continue' alone, so ruling 26 October's rule on the two save buttons does not reach it either. One plants defect the code shows is for the report: a Remove naming a line the collection does not hold is answered at 400 with no error message to the trader (repo-plantsfrontend-p4-031-m1).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p4-001 to -p4-037 and -p4-114 to -p4-125 show the list, its table, its banner, its floor and its single save control as they are today.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's per-line Commodity details page (its category question, the per-category fields genus, species, commodity code, variety, quantity, intended use, EPPO code, size of the trees and phytosanitary treatments, their hints, limits and errors, and its 'Continue', 'Save and continue' and 'Save and add another' buttons) stays as it is, keeping its 'About the consignment' caption.
requirements.why: Out of scope: no row in this area changes the plants Commodity details page, which shares the animals page's heading but asks plants' own per-line questions; the animals caption 'Description of the goods' follows Design Release 2.1's animals sections, which plants does not share in the form plants has it. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon changes plants only where a row changes a page or behaviour plants also has, and plants keeps its own questions, answers, sections, step order and data. Where plants already follows the same pattern (removing a line at once with no confirmation, keeping entered values after an error, carrying the change context), it stays as it is. The page offers no 'Save and return to overview', so ruling 26 October's rule on the two save buttons does not reach it. Plants defects the code shows are for the report, not this programme: a posted line index the collection no longer holds is appended as a new line instead of being refused (repo-plantsfrontend-p4-083), a quantity has no upper limit and is stored as the text typed (-p4-066, -p4-066-m1), a tree size is not checked as a number (-p4-074), and a failed line save is logged without naming the line (-p4-146).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p4-038 to -p4-092 and -p4-126 to -p4-151 show the page, its category question, its nine per-line fields, their hints, caps and messages, and its save controls as they are today.

requirements.statement: A number of animals above 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 is refused with an error naming that figure on that species' number of animals field, and the service that stores the count holds a whole number that large.
requirements.why: The data fields page caps the number of animals at that whole number and the data dictionary decides a field's limits, so the real service must accept every count the specification allows and refuse only what it cannot store.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a number of animals above 2,147,483,647 is refused with 'Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer' and exactly 2,147,483,647 is accepted, because that is the largest whole number the service storing it holds (repo-frontend-p10-045, -p10-046, -p10-166, repo-tests-p1-081, -p1-082).

requirements.statement: On Commodity details the number of animals and the number of packages are each asked once for every chosen species, in that species' own block.
requirements.why: Ruling 27 November keeps the default of the question this rested on: each chosen species under a commodity keeps its own number of animals and its own number of packages, as the real service's commodity line (one commodity plus one species) and Design Release 2.1 both have it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-088 posts one numberOfAnimalsQuantity and numberOfPackages pair per commodity line, and repo-frontend-p10-037 and -p10-039 ask both fields of every species line.

requirements.statement: The commodity page shows the service's page-maturity banner while its behaviour is still being detailed, and Commodity details, whose behaviour is agreed, shows none.
requirements.why: The service marks each page's maturity so a reviewer can see what has been agreed; Design Release 2.1 has no such banner because the prototype does not model maturity. Commodity details being agreed also makes it a signed-off page, so a change to its agreed behaviour needs a person.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-002 marks Commodity details agreed, so it renders no banner, and -p10-004 marks the identification page still being detailed.

requirements.statement: A number inside a quantity error message is written with thousands separators in the UK style, so 2147483647 reads as 2,147,483,647.
requirements.why: A trader reads the limit the message names, and an unseparated ten-digit number is hard to read.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-049 formats the maximum quantity with UK thousands separators for both above-maximum messages, in English and in Welsh.

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a quantity field on Commodity details saves the page and moves on, rather than pressing a row's Remove button.
requirements.why: A trader who finishes typing a count and presses Enter must not lose a commodity, which the removal buttons sitting before the fields would otherwise do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-065 and -p10-164 show Enter in a quantity field saving the page and moving on to identification details, because the form opens with a hidden Save and continue ahead of every Remove button.

requirements.statement: On a phone the Selected commodities table stays inside the screen width.
requirements.why: The table has three columns and a row action, and a trader on a phone must be able to read it without scrolling the page sideways.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-068 checks the table stays within the screen width on a phone today.

requirements.statement: The identification details page, its heading and inset, what happens to a line's identifier records when its count is raised, and any cap on how many commodity lines or identifier records a notification holds.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: this area stops at animal identification, so the identification page's own content and what happens to a line's records when its count is raised belong to the identification and permanent address area. No source asks for a cap on lines or records beyond each line's own number of animals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-003, -p10-069 and -p10-070 show the identification page as it is today, -p10-161 that nothing caps the lines or records, and -p10-162 that neither page says what a raised count does to the records already saved.

requirements.statement: Wherever Commodity details and identification details name a chosen species (the Selected commodities Species cell, the species sub-heading, the Remove button's hidden text and the count-drop error), it reads '<common name> (<Latin name>)', for example 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', or the Latin name alone when the species has no common name or its common name repeats the commodity name or the Latin name; a species with no Latin name held shows its common name alone.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names a species by its common name with the Latin name in brackets, and drops the common name where it would only repeat the commodity's name; one species label serves every place the two pages name a species.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a species is labelled with its Latin name and its common name in brackets ('Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle)'), the Latin name alone when no common name is held, and nothing at all when no Latin name is held, in every heading, table cell and message on both pages (repo-frontend-p10-013, -p10-014, -p10-017, repo-tests-p1-077, -p1-078).

requirements.statement: On Commodity details the Number of animals, Number of packages and germinal Quantity (unit/pieces) fields are GOV.UK text inputs ten characters wide, with a numeric keypad.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sizes every count field at width 10.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both live-animal fields are numeric inputs five characters wide (govuk-input--width-5, trace-animals-fit-p9-025, -p9-027; repo-frontend-p10-038 calls the field narrow).

requirements.statement: Commodity details lays its content out in the full-width grid column.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the page the full width, which holds the Selected commodities table's three columns and its row action.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page sits in a two-thirds grid column (trace-animals-fit-p9-076).

requirements.statement: The notification status strip above the caption shows the 'Draft' tag followed by the notification's type and reference, '<type> - <reference>': 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-0FI8DO' in the live-animals set and 'Germinal products - <reference>' in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the kind of notification the trader chose beside its reference on every journey page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows the 'Draft' tag and the reference in bold, with no notification type (trace-animals-fit-p9-005).

requirements.statement: When Commodity details is shown with errors its browser title begins 'Error: ', and each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern tells screen-reader users at once that the page has errors; the prototype's unprefixed title is prototype markup, not a design.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-060 shows the 'Error: ' title prefix and -p9-058 the hidden inline prefix today.

requirements.statement: A Remove post naming an entry the selection no longer holds shows Commodity details as it now stands, or the commodity page when nothing is left, and one naming a single species under a code whose species are not listed individually is refused as a bad request.
requirements.why: A stale page or a second tab must not break the page or remove the wrong line.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-026, -p10-027 and -p10-027-m1 show the refusal, the page shown as it stands with a warning logged, and the hop to the commodity question when the selection is empty.

requirements.statement: The Welsh wording of Commodity details and identification details, including the Welsh count-drop message's plural forms.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the Welsh copy is a machine draft marked not to be shown to users before Welsh Language Standards sign-off, and Design Release 2.1 has no Welsh. That the Welsh count-drop message does not singularise its counts is for the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-158 to -p10-160 show the Welsh bundle as it is today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics behind Commodity details: its form field names (numberOfPackages reused for the germinal quantity, germinalPackages, the removeCommodity and removeSpecies keys), its hidden from=hub marker, its session storage, the totals it works out for other pages, the package type it clears on save, its /design-release-2.1 mount, and how the real page names its own fields and hands species over from the commodity page.
requirements.why: Out of scope: field names, data shapes, paths and code structure are the real service's architecture, which the prototype never decides, and no increment changes an existing real path or code structure to match it. The real service keeps its own per-line field names and storage.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-072 shows the real commodity page handing species over in its own shape today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's germinal commodity catalogue content (its 18 embryo, ova and semen entries and their codes) as a source of which germinal commodities Commodity details shows.
requirements.why: Out of scope: commodity and species names and codes are a reference list, MDM's content reaching the service through reference-data, never edited in code to match the prototype; the prototype's app/data catalogue is a demo fixture.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, Commodity details lets a blank field pass and flags only an entered value that is not valid.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a template leave answers for the trader to fill in later. The templates rows are parked in their own theme, so this is built with them.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's Commodity details has the same back link, caption, heading, Selected commodities table and commodity groups as the live-animals page, with one table row per germinal commodity listing all its chosen species (for example '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'), each group headed '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)' such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and a section break between the species sections inside a germinal commodity group.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin plus Design Release 2.1's germinal differences, and Design Release 2.1 separates germinal species within a commodity.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set each species asks 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' in a text field with no hint, and no number of animals. It is required ('Enter the quantity') and must be a whole number of 1 or more ('Enter a whole number greater than 0'), each error shown in the summary and above that species' field and linked to it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the germinal count as 'Quantity (unit/pieces)', the name the data fields page gives the one mandatory germinal field, held on each commodity line.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set each species whose commodity the data fields page's package-count list names (its semen, embryo and ova lines) also asks 'Number of packages', after Quantity (unit/pieces), with no hint and no '(when required)'. It is optional, but a value given must be a whole number of 1 or more, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number greater than 0', linked to that species' field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal species an optional package count with its own message, and the data fields page decides which commodities a package count applies to.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's Commodity details asks one 'Temperature' question for the consignment, after all commodity groups behind a section break: radios with the legend 'Temperature' at label size, the hint 'How the products will be stored.' and the options 'Ambient', 'Chilled' and 'Frozen' in that order. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the storage temperature once for a germinal consignment, and ruling 2026-10-09 makes the germinal set always ask it; the data fields page makes it optional.

requirements.statement: On the germinal products set's Commodity details the error summary lists errors by question, all species for one question before the next, in the order the questions appear in a species block: every quantity error before any number of packages error.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 orders the error summary by field type, as the live-animals page does; the temperature is optional and raises no error.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set Commodity details asks each species' total gross weight in that species' block, and a valid Save and continue reached in the journey goes on to the next page the journey puts after Commodity details, with no page for the consignment's total gross weight between them.
requirements.why: Ruling 27 November keeps the germinal set's total gross weight per species, while Design Release 2.1 now asks one total gross weight for the consignment on a page of its own after Commodity details; which is built waits on the owner, and this is the default.

conflicts.about: Whether Commodity details ends with the three return controls: DR1's application of rule (b) listed it among the primary-button-only pages; Design Release 2.1 and today give it all three.

positions.says: Rule (b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls.
Under inc-161, consignment details ends with the primary button alone.
Commodity details uses the shared journey actions: Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview.
Commodity details ends with Save and continue, Save and return to overview and Cancel and return to overview.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's rule (b), the highest-ranked judgement, is followed. In Design Release 2.1 the overview's task list links to both the commodity page and Commodity details, so rule (b) gives both the three controls (req-120). DR1's page list applied the rule to DR1's journey, where consignment details was reached from another page; it is not overruled, because it ranks above the prototype, and the rule itself is what governs.

conflicts.about: Opening Commodity details, or later pages, with no commodity chosen: Design Release 2.1's guards never redirect; the real page sends the trader to the commodity page.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence or validation, overrides the prototype.
The origin, commodity, import reason, consignment details and identifier guards all do nothing.
Opening the commodity details page when nothing is selected takes the trader to the commodity question instead.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the prototype's guards are stubs, not a design, and a real notification cannot hold quantities for commodities it does not have, so the Commodity details redirect stays (req-109).

conflicts.about: Validation of the live-animal number of packages: Design Release 2.1 accepts any value; the real page accepts blank or a whole number of 1 or more.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation, overrides the prototype.
The live-animal packages field is not validated and may hold any value.
A number of packages below one, a decimal or words are refused with 'Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5'.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the field stays optional as Design Release 2.1 has it, but the real service validates what it stores (req-113). The optional part of Design Release 2.1 is still cited through trace-prototype-dr2-1-p4-025 and prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-012.

conflicts.about: The page's path: Design Release 2.1's /design-release-2.1/consignment-details under its mirror mount and its ?category= start, or the real set's consignment-details journey page.

positions.says: The consignment details page is served at /design-release-2.1/consignment-details.
Every Design Release 2.1 route sits under the /design-release-2.1 mount.
A germinal products notification can be started directly at /create-notification?category=germinal-products.
The commodity details page is reached inside a notification journey at the slug consignment-details.
No increment changes an existing real URL path or code structure to match the prototype.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the page keeps its real path in each set's journey (req-118), and the prototype's paths, its mount and its ?category= start are not copied.

conflicts.about: Whether numbers typed on Commodity details but not yet saved survive a Remove.

positions.says: Numbers typed into a surviving commodity's fields but not yet saved are kept on the page after another commodity is removed.
The remove form does not carry unsaved typed counts, so the remaining species' inputs come back empty.
What a trader typed is never dropped.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling wins, and the frontend now keeps what the trader has typed: the numbers are still in their fields when Commodity details comes back, and a surviving line the post names no count for shows its stored value (req-1759). The trace of the empty inputs is not overruled, because it records the earlier behaviour that requirement's delta cites.

conflicts.about: The largest number of animals a species line accepts: the data fields page's 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, or the 2,147,483,647 the service that stores the count holds.

positions.says: V4 is the source of truth for data, and V4 also wins on shape, though how the shape is held in code is the frontend's own call.
The largest number of animals or packages the service accepts is 2,147,483,647, the largest whole number the service that stores it holds.
A number of animals above 2,147,483,647 is refused with 'Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer'.

conflicts.outcome: The data fields page wins: it ranks above the repos and decides a field's limits, capping the number of animals at 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, and ruling 11 November makes V4 win on shape as well as value, leaving how the shape is held in code to the services. So the number of animals accepts every whole number up to that figure, the service that stores it widens the whole number it holds, and the message names that figure (req-2132). The repo claims are not overruled: they record today's cap, which that requirement's delta cites, and the ten-digit cap stays the right one for the number of packages while c-325 is open.

conflicts.about: Which commodities get the Number of packages question: the nine Design Release 2.1 gives packaging fields, or every commodity the data fields page's package-count list names.

positions.says: Every other live-animal commodity in the catalogue, 39 of the 48, shows only Number of animals, with no packages field.
For chickens the commodity block asks only for Number of animals.
V4 is the source of truth for data: no row may rest on the prototype's app/data files for which commodities a rule covers.
The number of packages field is shown only for the commodity codes the frontend's own applicability rules name.

conflicts.outcome: Ruling 11 November wins: which commodities a rule covers is V4's, and the prototype's packaging list comes from its demo catalogue. The question is asked wherever the data fields page's package-count list names the species' commodity, poultry and the semen, embryo and ova lines included, in both sets (req-112), as c-324 already settled for the earlier prototype's claims. repo-frontend-p10-040 is not overruled: it records today's rules, which req-112's delta cites. prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-026 is not a position here, because it still carries the field's label and hint.

conflicts.about: Whether Commodity details' browser title gains 'Error: ' when the page has errors: Design Release 2.1 leaves it unchanged; the real page prefixes it.

positions.says: The browser title stays the same when commodity details is shown with errors, with no 'Error: ' prefix.
In the error state the browser title is prefixed 'Error: '.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default.
The prototype's code is not accessible and not production grade, being prototype code rather than GDS components.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings win: the GOV.UK error pattern's title prefix is an accessibility behaviour the prototype's markup does not express, so the real page keeps 'Error: ' in its title.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal Commodity details page asks a total gross weight for each species, or none, with the consignment's total gross weight asked once on a page of its own after it.

positions.says: In the germinal products set, the number of packages and the total gross weight stay per species.
Commodity details asks no weight for any species: the consignment's total gross weight is asked on its own page after it.
The total gross weight page is titled 'What is the total gross weight of the consignment?'.
A valid germinal Commodity details page continues to the total gross weight page.

conflicts.outcome: The two readings build different pages and nothing ranks them on this point: the 27 November ruling outranks the prototype, but it kept the default of a question about one count per commodity against one per species, and its clause on weight speaks to that granularity, not to which page asks the weight. The prototype, given after it moved on, asks one consignment weight on its own page. It goes to the owner with the ruling's words as the default.
conflicts.question: Does the germinal products set ask a total gross weight for each species on Commodity details, as the 27 November ruling's kept default says, or one total gross weight for the whole consignment on its own page after Commodity details, as Design Release 2.1 now has it?
conflicts.default: Germinal products: Commodity details asks each species' total gross weight in that species' block, because the 27 November ruling ranks above the prototype and keeps the weight per species, and no page for the consignment's total gross weight is built, so Save and continue goes on to the next page after Commodity details. Live animals: unaffected, it asks no weight.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal temperature is required on Commodity details (Design Release 2.1) or optional (the data fields page).

positions.says: When shown, storage temperature is required: none chosen shows 'Select a temperature'.
Quantity and Temperature are required: both empty shows 'Enter the quantity' and 'Select a temperature'.
Continuing with nothing filled shows 'Enter the quantity' and 'Select a temperature'.
V4 is the source of truth for data.

conflicts.outcome: V4 wins, as c-232 already settled for the earlier prototype: whether a germinal field is mandatory is data, the data fields page makes Temperature optional and the quantity the one mandatory field. So Temperature raises no error when unanswered and does not hold back the task's Complete status (req-1763), while the quantity's blank error stands through prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-086. prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-099 is not overruled, because it still backs the quantity condition and the live-animals condition; only its temperature clause is set aside.
